title: Adaptive column elasticity and contextual sort affordances for large virtual tables
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary: Introduce an adaptive column elasticity model plus contextual sort/filter affordances to improve usability of very wide virtualized tables. This ticket covers design exploration, accessibility requirements, prototype Figma screens, and a handoff package for Engineering to implement a progressive renderer that supports per-column elasticity heuristics and on-hover sort hints.

Problem: Users struggle with extremely wide datasets where rigid column widths cause important attributes to be clipped or push critical controls off-screen. Existing resize handles are not discoverable in high-density modes, and sort/filter affordances are buried under overflow menus when columns compress. This results in support tickets, slower triage flows, and higher time-to-action for customers building observability and data-grid UIs.

Goal: Deliver a design that: 1) automatically classes columns into elasticity tiers (fixed, flexible, compressible), 2) surfaces lightweight contextual sort/filter hints on hover or keyboard focus without increasing render cost, 3) plays nicely with the runtime's progressive virtualization (windowing) and cache reuse, and 4) is keyboard accessible and screen-reader friendly.
acceptance_criteria: Design spec with explicit elasticity rules for at least 3 column archetypes (id/primary, metric, free-text)
Figma prototype with hover and focus states demonstrating contextual sort/filter affordances
Annotated accessibility notes: keyboard walkthrough, aria roles for resize handles and sort controls
Engineering handoff doc listing events, telemetry keys, and recommended thresholds for progressive virtualization
Design token updates documented for spacing and hit targets in compact/dense modes
design_notes: Elasticity tiers: primary columns = fixed min 120px, flexible columns = flex-grow with min 80px, compressible columns = truncated with ellipsis and accessible detail view
Spacing token adjustments: increase interactive hit target from 24px to 28px in dense mode for resize affordances to reduce input errors on touchpads
Hover affordance: lightweight chevron + hint (sort asc/desc) appears on column header after 180ms hover; keyboard focus shows persistent control
Progressive virtualization compatibility: affordances must be rendered using a shallow overlay layer so header virtualization window can recycle DOM without reattaching heavy listeners
Performance trade-off: replace continuous mousemove listeners with pointerenter/pointerleave + debounced hover to avoid dragging down render in 2000+ row tables
decisions: Use three elasticity tiers to balance predictability and responsiveness
Show sort affordances on hover (180ms delay) and immediately on keyboard focus to satisfy accessibility
Avoid attaching affordance logic to every header cell; use event delegation on header row to reduce listeners
Do not introduce new global layout shifts; leverage transform-based overlays for visual affordances
risks: Complexity of elasticity heuristics could cause unexpected relayouts when users resize containers; mitigate with clear animations and stable heuristics
Edge-case interactions with pinned/sticky columns need validation across browsers (Safari sticky behavior has known quirks)
Potential conflicts with existing KV cache and batching logic in runtime; engineering to validate memory/DOM footprint
tasks: Design: finalize Figma prototype for Compact/Dense/Comfortable density modes
Accessibility: write keyboard-only flow and aria label copy with accessibility engineer
Research: run 5 quick usability sessions with internal PMs using prototype
Engineering: create spike branch implementing overlay affordances and elasticity algorithm (ENG- spike TBD)
QA: create test matrix for resizing, virtualization window jumps, and screen-reader announcements

release_notes: Introduce tiered column elasticity and contextual header affordances to improve discoverability and reduce horizontal scrolling in wide datasets.
implementation_guidance: Event strategy: attach a single pointerenter/leave handler to header row and compute target header via event.target.closest('[data-header-cell]')
Overlay rendering: use a top-level overlay container appended to table root to avoid DOM churn during virtualization swaps
Performance thresholds: disable hover affordance animation under clientWidth < 600px or when row count > 10k by default
